subject.title: enhancement: Optimize voice message processing pipeline for Telegram

question: What Telegram voice pipeline contract should OpenClaw support before implementation: narrow early feedback, async/background TTS delivery, a priority voice lane, or a full staged STT/TTS pipeline with state snapshots?
rationale: The source gap is real, but the fix crosses Telegram ingress ordering, audio authorization/preflight, TTS delivery semantics, caching policy, and session-state visibility, so automation should not choose the permanent product contract.

options.title: Stage measured async STT/TTS design
options.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, use the narrower related issues for cue and delivery-policy slices, and require stage ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks before coding.

options.title: Limit to feedback and delivery
options.body: Treat immediate typing cues plus a future text/voice delivery policy as the near-term fixes while leaving deeper queueing, streaming, and caching unplanned for now.

options.title: Defer broad pipeline work
options.body: Keep current provider tuning and delivery semantics until maintainers have stronger live evidence that a staged voice pipeline is worth the complexity.

recommendation.title: Stage measured async STT/TTS design
recommendation.body: Keep this issue as the broad tracker, use the narrower related issues for cue and delivery-policy slices, and require stage ordering, state snapshots, and live benchmarks before coding.

likelyOwner.reason: This choice spans Telegram audio preflight and shared TTS runtime behavior, where the strongest combined history points to steipete.
